# No more scrolling up

When the agent refers back to an earlier section, it now tells you what that section was, right where it mentions it.

## What changed

- Recap on the spot. Whenever the agent mentions an earlier section or chapter, it recaps it in one sentence: its title, what you built and the idea it taught, such as "In section 2, Memory transfers, you copied an array to the GPU and back, because the GPU has its own memory." Then it says how that connects to what you are doing now. It never refers to a section by number alone, so you never have to scroll up to follow along.

## Upgrade

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace update no-vibe`, then restart.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade no-vibe`, then remove and add the plugin again.
- Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe` once 4.3.0 is on npm, or `pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- opencode: `opencode reload`.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v4.2.0...v4.3.0

# From input to output, with the reasons in the code

no-vibe now shows how each program turns its input into its output, and the code it gives you carries short comments that say why it is written that way.

## What changed

- Input to output. For every program or function the agent shows, it follows one real input through the code: what goes in, each step that changes it and the value after that step, and what comes out. It then points at what you will see when you run it and names the line that produced each part, so the output is never a surprise. Longer traces are drawn as a diagram.
- Comments in the code. Every example, exercise and build step has short comments that say why the code is written that way: what a block does to the data, what would break without a line, or why this approach and not the obvious one. Comments that only repeat the code are left out. You type the comments with the code, so after running it you can reread code and reasons together instead of going back and forth to the chat.

## Upgrade

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace update no-vibe`, then restart.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade no-vibe`, then remove and add the plugin again.
- Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe` once 4.2.0 is on npm, or `pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- opencode: `opencode reload`.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v4.1.0...v4.2.0

# From naive to real, and seeing the difference

no-vibe now builds each idea up from the simplest version you can write by hand, and lets you run the versions side by side to see what each step changed.

## What changed

- From naive to real. Each new idea starts at its most naive working version, written only with what you already know, such as plain arithmetic before a loop and a loop before a library. It then improves one step at a time until it reaches what people really use. Each step says what problem it fixes, what changed and how the two compare. The agent picks the steps from the topic, your level, your stack and the situation, and you write by hand what a library does before you use the library.
- See the difference. When two versions give the same output, the agent gives you a small probe to type and run on both, such as a timer, a count of steps or allocations, a much bigger input, or an edge case where the first version breaks, so you see the difference instead of just hearing about it.
- Teaching that adapts. The skill's teaching guidance is now a default. The agent follows it as far as it fits, and finds its own way when it does not fit you, the situation or the environment. The write guard, the header and your saved progress stay the same, and you still type every line.

## Upgrade

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace update no-vibe`, then restart.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade no-vibe`, then remove and add the plugin again.
- Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe` once 4.1.0 is on npm, or `pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- opencode: `opencode reload`.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v4.0.0...v4.1.0

# Roadmaps, and a lesson that fits how you learn

no-vibe now calls your lesson plan a roadmap, asks how you like to learn, and researches your goal before planning.

## Breaking change

The lesson file is now `.no-vibe/ROADMAP.md`, and the old `.no-vibe/syllabus.md` is no longer read. To keep a lesson in progress, run this in that project before you resume:

```bash
mv .no-vibe/syllabus.md .no-vibe/ROADMAP.md
```

The reply header step is now `roadmap` instead of `syllabus`.

## What changed

- Roadmap. The plan of chapters is called a roadmap everywhere, in the file name, the header and the wording.
- Your learning style, asked. The agent always asks how you want to learn, code first, explanation first, a mix, or your own way, instead of guessing. It then teaches in that order. Your notes in `## Notes` still win if they say otherwise.
- Research scoped to your goal. Before writing the roadmap, the agent looks for existing roadmaps toward the same goal, such as learning paths, course outlines or roadmap.sh, then searches for anything else your goal needs, as often as it takes. Every search stays on your goal. It checks its plan against what it found, adds missing prerequisites, drops what you do not need, and fixes the order. Other roadmaps are only used to find gaps, never copied.
- README. The lesson walkthrough now describes the roadmap, the learning style question, optional chapters and what is saved for a fresh session.

## Upgrade

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace update no-vibe`, then restart.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade no-vibe`, then remove and add the plugin again.
- Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe` once 4.0.0 is on npm, or `pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- opencode: `opencode reload`.

Then rename any lesson in progress, as shown above.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v3.6.0...v4.0.0

# Continue any lesson in a fresh session

no-vibe now keeps a record of each section in `syllabus.md`, so a new session, or a different agent, can pick up your lesson knowing what you have already learned. Your own instructions on how to teach are kept too.

## What changed

- Sections planned when a chapter begins. The agent plans the chapter's sections up front and lists them under the chapter in `syllabus.md`, then teaches them in order. It can still change the sections still to come based on how you are doing.
- A record of what you learned. When a section ends, the agent ticks it and writes two lines under it: `Core:`, the 1 to 3 things you must remember, and `Saw:`, how it went. Chapters get a `Check:` line with the check result, and skipped chapters or sections are marked.
- Your notes, kept. `## Notes` in `syllabus.md` now holds what you asked the agent to change in how it teaches, such as "Explain code with comments inside the code" or "Write less text". The agent follows every note on every turn, including after a fresh start.
- Resume uses both. When you run `/no-vibe on` in a new session, the agent reads the section record and your notes before it continues.

## Upgrade

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace update no-vibe`, then restart.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade no-vibe`, then remove and add the plugin again.
- Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe` once 3.6.0 is on npm, or `pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- opencode: `opencode reload`.

A lesson started on an earlier version still resumes. Its old notes stay where they are, and new sections are recorded the new way.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v3.5.1...v3.6.0
